answer: Adjacency Pulse Decay. Each agent emits a periodic pulse to its graph neighbors; an edge stays live only if both endpoints keep pulsing. New nodes join as small isolated islands, and their pulses count for routing weight only after receiving replies from distinct existing clusters. An attacker must run many real, responsive agents sustained across separate clusters, paying ongoing compute and coordination latency per identity; a cluster that stops answering loses its ember of trust and its edges decay.
